title: Comparing Two Places I Know

opts: тогда как / в то время как
prepTasks.correct: тогда как / в то время как

writingModel: Two Places I Know: Aktobe and Uralsk — by Rustam Seilov

I grew up in Aktobe and have now spent three years studying in Uralsk. Both cities are in western Kazakhstan, but they have remarkably different personalities. I've thought a lot about how they compare — and which one has felt more like home.

In terms of size, Aktobe is significantly larger than Uralsk. It has a bigger population, more shopping centres, and a wider variety of restaurants and entertainment options. The road infrastructure is also more developed. However, Uralsk is more compact, and I've found that easier to navigate. In Aktobe, everything is further apart — you need a car or a long bus ride to get anywhere. In Uralsk, I can walk to most places I need within twenty minutes.

When it comes to atmosphere, the two cities feel quite different. Aktobe is busier and noisier — especially in the city centre. Uralsk is quieter, and that has been better for my concentration and study habits. The pace of life here is slightly slower, and I've actually enjoyed that more than I expected.

The most significant difference, for me, is the sense of community. In Aktobe, I knew my neighbourhood well, but the city felt larger than any individual. In Uralsk, I know my professors by name, my local café owner recognises me, and my dormitory friends have become some of the closest people in my life. It's a smaller community, but a stronger one.

On the other hand, I miss some things about Aktobe. It has more cultural events — concerts, exhibitions, sports competitions. The selection of food is also better. Whereas Uralsk has a limited number of restaurants, Aktobe has cuisines from across Kazakhstan and beyond.

Overall, I think Uralsk has been the better choice for me as a student. It's not the most exciting city, and it doesn't have the most impressive facilities. But it has given me exactly what I needed: focus, community, and the feeling that I belong somewhere. That, I've decided, is more valuable than size or glamour.
